title: Spare Capacity Catalog and Runbook — weekly ops
content:
Purpose:
This is a working catalog and short runbook for how to treat 'spare' GPU capacity across regions when we need fast headroom for short bursts (canary ramps, QA smoke runs, emergency reroutes).

Why this doc:
- We lack a single reference for what counts as spare (preemptible vs reserved vs dedicated burst) and the quick actions SRE/oncall should take to expose that spare to production routes.
- Complement to the capacity hedging playbook: narrower, operational, and designed for <24h ops decisions.

Summary (high level):
- Define three spare-capacity classes (S1, S2, S3). Each class has different preemption risk and allowed latency impact.
- Provide quick checks (3 commands / dashboards) and a 6-step runbook to reclaim or expose spare capacity.
- Include routing knobs and recommended communication templates.

Spare capacity catalog (canonical):
- S1 — Low-risk reserved burst
  - Description: Reserved nodes held for burst by Dedicated customers; SLA-backed but can be throttled for internal spare allocation during emergency with approval.
  - Typical hardware: H100-80GB (west-us-2, eu-west-1), A100-80GB (ap-south-1 for dedicated pools)
  - Preemption risk: 0–5% (contracted)
  - Recommended uses: high-priority canaries, slow-roll experiments, small production fallbacks
  - Cost impact: high (bill to dedicated pool)

- S2 — Opportunistic preemptible pool (short lived)
  - Description: Preemptible/spot nodes that are normally used for training batch or background offline tasks; low-latency but can be reclaimed within minutes.
  - Typical hardware: A100-40GB, T4 in some regions (us-east-1, us-west-2)
  - Preemption risk: 10–60% (varies by region/time)
  - Recommended uses: non-SLA inference (low-priority routes), evictable background workloads, soak tests, internal QA ramps
  - Cost impact: low

- S3 — Elastic shared burst (managed local autoscaling buffer)
  - Description: Short-duration warmed instances with KV-prefix cache warmed and reduced batch sizes; used to absorb sudden <15s bursts.
  - Typical hardware: mixed; often smaller sequence length optimised cards (H100/A100)
  - Preemption risk: similar to S2 for infra policies; lower if pinned to zoned reserved nodes
  - Recommended uses: short spikes of production traffic; transient routing only (≤ 5 minutes)
  - Cost impact: moderate (warm+cache overhead)

Quick signals + dashboards to check (first 90s):
1) GPU-heatmap: /dashboards/fleet/heatmap — check available nodes filter by region, tag:spare_pool (green == idle slots)
2) preemptible-eviction-rate query: "sum(rate(preemptible.evictions[5m])) by (region)" — alert if >30 evictions/min in a region
3) route-latency SLO windows: last 5m p95 on low-priority routes (if p95 increases > 200ms, do not shift more load)

Runbook (fast action, <20 minutes):
1) Verify need: confirm traffic spike or canary/experiment requires spare capacity (owner: oncall).
2) Check S1 first: run `infra-cli list-pools --tag reserved-burst --region <r>` and validate owner approval. If S1 available, contact pool owner (Slack template below) then toggle route.
3) If no S1, evaluate S3 prewarm: `infra-cli prewarm --pool s3 --region <r> --ttl 5m --model <model>` (recommended TTL < 10m). Validate cache warm hit rate > 0.6 before diverting traffic.
4) If S3 not available, fallback to S2 with caution: `infra-cli route-allow --pool s2 --max-concurrency 0.2` (start with 20% of expected burst).
5) Monitor eviction and latency signals aggressively (dashboards above). If evictions spike or p95 > threshold, rollback immediately and open ENGINFRA incident.
6) Post-action: update this document and add a short note to the weekly ops log with metrics (evictions, cost delta, success/failure).

Command snippets (concrete):
- List spare nodes: `infra-cli nodes list --filter "tag:spare_pool" --fields region,gpu_type,status`
- Prewarm API (example): `curl -X POST https://api.redwood/ops/prewarm -d '{"pool":"s3","region":"eu-west-1","model":"rwd-base-13b","ttl":300}'`
- Route toggle example: `infra-cli routing update --route infer-low-prio --add-pool s3 --weight 0.15`

Communication templates (Slack + Incident):
- Slack quick ping to pool owner: "Hey @<owner>, we need temporary access to reserved-burst (S1) in <region> for ~10m to handle a canary ramp (ticket ENGINFRA-XXXX). Are you ok to grant?"
- Incident title template: "[PG:GPU-SPARE] Eviction spike after routing to S2 — <region> — <time>"

Simulation notes (dry-run 7/27):
- Setup: 30-min simulated canary (rwd-base-7b) in us-west-2, attempted to use S3 prewarm pool for 8m; started at 09:10 UTC.
- Observations: prewarm warmed KV cache to ~0.7 hit rate in 90s; p50 latency stable; after 4m we saw two evictions in sibling hosts but no service degradation.
- Cost: approx +$12 for prewarm time.
- Lessons: prefer small prewarm durations (≤10m). For canaries >2k tokens/min, use S1 or reserve a micro-slice of S1 ahead of time.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Q1: Can we expose a programmatic soft-approval flow for S1 (owner auto-ack for <10m allocations)? Owner: Rina — investigate policy + billing implications.
- Q2: Should the prewarm API surface a 'warm-score' (cache hit prediction) so we can programmatically gate routing? Owner: Diego.
- Q3: Do we want a per-customer 'spare-cushion' SLA flag that prevents spills into dedicated pools without explicit approval? Product input needed — @product-hosted-api.

Action items (this week):
- A1: Rina: prototype owner-ack flow for S1 and list billing constraints — due 2026-08-06.
- A2: Diego: add warm-score metric to prewarm API and mock in staging — due 2026-08-03.
- A3: Evan: add a small runbook test to next Friday's chaos window (exercise S2 fallback) — due 2026-08-06.
- A4: Aisha: consolidate post-mortem template for spare-pool ops and add to weekly log — due 2026-08-02.

Notes to self / messy thoughts (working):
- We should add region-weight heuristics (prefer low-eviction zones for S2; prefer reserved single-tenant hosts for S1).
- Consider tagging pools with 'warm_profile: short|long' so UI can show estimated warm time.
- Need clearer cost reporting per spare-use: show prewarm and evictions as separate line items in console.
- If we do automated soft-approve for S1, guardrails must include: max_minutes=10, max_weight=0.25, billing_alert_to_owner=true.

Appendix — quick metrics snapshot (7/27 dry-run):
- Region: us-west-2
- S1 available nodes: 2 (H100)
- S3 prewarm instances spun: 4 (avg warm time 95s)
- Evictions during test: 2
- p95 latency delta during test: +40ms (stable)
- Cost delta (estimated): $12

References:
- Related playbook: https://redwood-confluence/internal/capacity-hedging-playbook
- Jira: ENGINFRA-4823 (spare-pool telemetry), ENGINFRA-4879 (prewarm API enhancements)

If you're reading this and have a better short checklist, please edit inline — this doc is intended to be nimble.

-- Aisha
